global_notes: Candidate landing sites (CLS) are manually selected representatives and can be shifted within the suitable area (Wueller 2026, Section 3).
130 CLS were studied across 16 candidate regions.

Region boundary polygons were not found in the dataset description read. Zenodo Landing_Sites is described as holding candidate-site points and a raster of the area meeting HLS requirements; check the files before relying on region outlines.
CRS and longitude convention were not confirmed from retrieved text; do not reproject until verified.
Site IDs ending in K2023 (NR2_K2023, HW_K2023) appear in Table A1 alongside numbered sites. Whether they are among the representative sites counted in Table 1 is unverified.

sites.coordinate_type: specific_candidate_landing_site_point (manually selected representative, NOT region boundary)
site_notes: Listed among SP sites with accessible PSRs <110 K (PSR accessibility table; table number not confirmed).
Lies within a landing area suggested by Samaddar et al. (2025) as free of large boulders in Mini-RF radar data, per Wueller et al. 2026.

scientific_advantages: Highest fractional area meeting HLS slope criteria among the 16 regions studied (Wueller 2026, Section 3).
scientific_limitations: Slope criteria do not establish landing safety.
Region-level figures only; not site-level terrain statistics.
